questions.prompt: Does the Follow button get rounded corners?

options.text: No: the real `<button>` is in PrimeNG's template, so this component's styles don't reach it
Only after the page is refreshed

questions.explanation: With emulated encapsulation, a component's styles apply only to its own template. Set a token instead, for example `--p-button-border-radius: 8px;` on `.follow-button`, or pass `[dt]`.

options.text: Follow is blue, Share keeps the theme's primary color

questions.explanation: CSS variables are inherited, and encapsulation doesn't stop that. The variable is set on `.follow-button` only, so only the button inside it picks it up.

questions.prompt: Aura defines `primary.color` separately for light and dark mode. What color are the primary buttons with this preset?

code.label: app-preset.ts

options.text: Still Aura's green: the value under `colorScheme` wins over a plain value

questions.explanation: When the preset defines a token under `colorScheme.light` and `colorScheme.dark`, your override must use the same structure: `semantic: { colorScheme: { light: { primary: { color: '#0095f6' } }, dark: { ... } } }`.

questions.prompt: The app is configured like this, and a trainee's laptop is set to dark mode. What does the feed look like?

code.label: app.config.ts

options.text: PrimeNG components turn dark, while our own components stay light

questions.explanation: By default PrimeNG follows the operating system with `prefers-color-scheme`. Our SCSS doesn't, so the page mixes both. Add `options: { darkModeSelector: false }` when the design has no dark mode.

questions.explanation: The class does reach the label, but this component's rules only match elements in its own template. Use `pt` for attributes like `aria-label` or `data-*`, and tokens or CSS variables for styling.

questions.prompt: The design uses rounder buttons everywhere in the app. Where do you change it?
questions.explanation: A change for the whole app belongs in the preset: `components: { button: { root: { borderRadius: '8px' } } }`. Use `[dt]` or CSS variables for one place, and never `::ng-deep`.
